info.title: nac-web HTTP API
info.description: Live OpenAPI 3.1 contract for nac-web's REST and SSE surface. nac-web binds to loopback by default. Non-loopback binds require --allow-remote and an authenticated, encrypted network boundary; every reachable client receives control equivalent to the local user because the API has no client authentication. IP-literal Host values bypass only the DNS-name allowlist, not authentication. DNS names must be listed in NAC_ALLOWED_HOSTS. Cross-origin browser mutations are rejected independently. Finite JSON responses may be gzip-compressed. The SSE stream is text/event-stream and is never gzip-compressed. Credential values are write-only. /mcp is streamable-HTTP MCP (JSON-RPC), not REST, and is intentionally out of band.

post.summary: Validate a credential by asking its provider which models it may use.
post.description:
A key arrives in the request body and is forwarded once; it is never stored
by this route, and the destination goes through the same credential trust
check as a session launch. A provider signed in through the browser has no
key to send, so the stored login answers instead — and its answer is the
same evidence the launch UI needs that the login still works.

oneOf.description:
A configured MCP server that could not be loaded for a worker, reported
with a bounded, credential-redacted reason so the user can see why the
server's tools are missing.

A model call the provider itself refused, reported with credentials
redacted.

Ordinary errors are reduced to a constant before they leave the process,
because their text can carry paths and tool output. What a provider says
about its own API — no credits, bad key, rate limit, context too long —
carries none of that and is the one thing the user has to see to act, so
it travels intact apart from credential material, which is masked before
the event leaves the process. Live-only, like the other events whose
absence keeps the persisted stream readable by older builds.

AssistantStreamDelta.description:
A slice of model output as it is being produced. Rides its own channel
rather than [`SessionEvent`]: deltas arrive an order of magnitude more
often than session events, they are worthless the moment the assistant
message lands, and pushing them through the sequenced bus would evict the
replay ring a reconnecting client depends on. So no sequence id, no replay,
no persistence — a subscriber that falls behind just misses text it is about
to receive in full anyway.

AuthStatus.description:
Whether a provider has a usable credential right now, as served by
`GET /models`. A picker HINT only — it never changes how auth works:
API-key providers still read only the exact `api_key_env` selector and
managed providers still read only their stored credential file.

current.description: None on a detached HEAD or in a repository without commits.

dirty.description: Tracked files differ from HEAD, which makes switching unsafe.

parent.description: `None` at a filesystem root, which is where upward navigation stops.

path.description: Canonical path of the listed directory.

message_idx.description: Transcript index of the assistant message to project through.

target_behavior.description:
The other session type. Agent sources continue in NAC; NAC sources
continue in Agent.

CostTier.description:
One context-priced rate step (models.dev `cost.tiers[]` with
`tier.type == "context"`): applies when the response's prompt tokens
(input + cache read + cache write) exceed `input_tokens_above`. Rates
are complete — mappers fill buckets a tier omits from the base rates, so
selection is a wholesale swap.

base_url.description: Defaults to the provider's canonical URL.

behavior.description:
Immutable execution behavior. Omission preserves the established
orchestrator default.

extra_headers.description: Prefer a JSON object. A JSON-encoded object string remains accepted for compatibility.

first_chat.description:
Marks the required first chat for an empty project. The server
serializes this admission and returns the already-created primary chat
to concurrent callers instead of creating a duplicate. Ordinary New
Chat requests leave this false.

light_model.description: Light worker model; omitted or null launches single-model.

orchestrator_compaction_threshold.description: Omitted defaults to 70% of the model's context window; null or zero disables.

project_id.description: Explicit project selection. Projects are never inferred from `cwd`.

ssh_host.description: OpenSSH target for remote sessions; `cwd` is remote and defaults to `~`.

ssh_port.description:
Port and private key for the ssh target. Both are optional: omitted
leaves the choice to ssh, which is what a host configured in
`~/.ssh/config` wants. Supplying them is what lets a session reach a box
nac has no config for at all.

DefaultLimits.description:
A provider `_default` entry's limits and effort support, as served by
`GET /models`: powers the frontend's unrecognized-model badge, estimated
context gauge and custom-model effort list without a second resolve call.

deleted_session_ids.description: Sessions deleted along with the project.

released_session_ids.description: Sessions that stayed behind and are now unassigned.

DeleteProjectSessions.description: What a project delete does with the chats inside it.

login_id.description: Handle for polling this login; it names nothing on disk.

user_code.description:
Present only when the flow leaves something to read out: Codex's device
flow expects it typed, Arcee's asks for it to be checked against the
page, and the redirect flow has nothing to show at all.

oneOf.description: The provider has not seen the user approve it yet.

status.description:
`ok` for a retained handoff, otherwise how the dispatch died. Snapshots
written before dispatch outcomes were recorded only held handoffs.

EpisodeStatus.description:
How a dispatch ended.

Only [`EpisodeStatus::Ok`] episodes are retained context: they are the ones
a later dispatch reads back and the ones `thread_read` renders. The failure
kinds exist so the panel can still show what a thread was asked to do and
how it died, which is otherwise lost the moment the worker is killed.

message_idx.description:
Transcript index of the assistant message to fork from. Trailing tool
results that belong to that turn are copied with it.

configured_model.description:
Configured model id; lets the launch dialog render the inherited
"from config" selection resolved against the model catalog (the
frontend resolves the provider from the model id, exactly like
session creation does).

ssh_host.description: OpenSSH target for remote sessions; remote paths never select local config.

LightModelSettings.description:
The optional light worker model of a session. `Some` on a session enables
weight-classified dispatch: light dispatches run this model, heavy
dispatches run the orchestrator's own model. The model remains a catalog
id; backend and reasoning effort are typed before entering the domain
model, and the credential is always a selector name, never a key value.

ManagedAuthProvider.description: A provider that authenticates from a browser login rather than an API key.

backend.description: The backend a session selects to use this login.

oneOf.description:
Delegated sessions remain addressable by id, but clients use lineage
to keep them out of primary chat navigation and enforce ownership UI.

McpLibraryAuth.description: What a library server needs before it can connect.

McpLibraryEntry.description:
One catalog entry. Every field feeds the add-server form: the entry is a
pre-fill, never a hidden configuration — what is saved is exactly what the
form shows.

auth_header.description: Header the form should prompt for, when auth wants one.

auth_hint.description: Hint shown next to the header input, e.g. the expected value shape.

category.description: Section the picker groups the entry under before a search.

icon_url.description: Thumbnail shown next to the entry in the picker.

id.description: Stable identifier, recorded on servers created from the entry.

name.description: Display name; also the default server name.

tags.description:
Search fallback terms: consulted when a query matches neither name
nor description.

transport.description:
All current entries are `streamable_http`; stdio ones may appear
later.

McpProbedTool.description: A tool a probe discovered on a server, before anything is saved.

McpServerView.description:
A saved server as the dashboard sees it: env and header values are
redacted, everything else round-trips.

duration_ms.description:
Wall-clock time the model call behind this message took. Only ever
read by the UI: every provider mapper drops it, so it never travels
back out on the wire.

oneOf.description:
The model that produced this message (S5). Stamped at the
transcript push site; `None` on pre-S5 (legacy) messages, which
the wire normalization treats as same-model. Drives the
same-model reasoning-replay gate in `model::normalize_history`.

reasoning_field.description:
The wire field that carried `reasoning_text` on completions
endpoints ("reasoning_content" vs "reasoning"); replayed under
the same name. `None` for details-based reasoning (Anthropic,
OpenAI Responses) and legacy messages.

ModelConfigurationRecord.description:
A named, reusable model setup offered by the launch modal.

`api_key_env` names the credential rather than holding it: the value lives
in the credential store (or the environment), exactly as it does for a
configuration written by hand in `config.toml`.

initial_prompt.description: Message the launch modal pre-fills when this setup is chosen.

oneOf.description: Light worker model; `None` keeps single-model behavior.

orchestrator_compaction_threshold.description:
Compaction budget a session started from this setup inherits; `None`
falls back to `[compaction].threshold_tokens`.

ModelCostRates.description:
Cost rates in USD per 1M tokens. All-zero = unknown (pi's zero-cost
fallback); `calculate_cost` bills unknown pricing as zero. Missing fields
deserialize as zero so partial catalog records stay loadable.

`tiers` carries context-dependent pricing (models.dev `cost.tiers`,
pi's `model.cost.tiers`): when a response's prompt size exceeds a tier's
`input_tokens_above`, that tier's rates replace the base rates for the
response. `None` and `Some([])` both mean flat pricing; the Option keeps
user overrides three-state (absent = keep existing tiers, `[]` = clear).

ModelEntry.description:
One real catalog entry as served by `GET /models` (never a
ProviderDefault/Fallback synthesis product).

ModelListing.description: The full catalog listing served by `GET /models`.

catalog_version.description:
Monotonic version of the process-global catalog, bumped on every
reload (the initial load is version 1). Debugging/future-staleness
surface only; v1 attaches no cache semantics.

ModelOrigin.description:
Identifies the model that produced an assistant message (S5 reasoning
discipline). Reasoning signatures (Anthropic thinking blocks, OpenAI
reasoning items, completions reasoning text) are only replayed to the
same origin; a different origin makes the wire normalization strip them.

ModelSource.description:
Where the metadata for a resolved model came from. Served by the
`/models` listing (snake_case wire names) — the frontend badges
user-overridden and unrecognized (provider-default) models from it.

fell_back_to_parent.description: True when the requested file was missing and its parent was opened.

opened.description: Absolute path handed to the OS opener.

ProjectRecord.description:
Stable project projection shared by persistence, managed workflows, and
delivery without exposing a SQLite implementation.

ProviderAuth.description:
How a provider authenticates, as served by `GET /models`: auth
*requirements* (drives picker field visibility and hints), not status.

ProviderListing.description: One provider group in the `GET /models` listing.

auth_hint.description:
The conventional credential env var name (API-key providers) or the
login command (managed providers) when `auth_status` is
`no_credential`; `None` when ready or when no conventional name is
known.

auth_status.description:
Computed per request from the process environment and the managed
credential files — never baked into the catalog.

default_base_url.description:
The provider's catalog endpoint default (models.dev `api` or the
curated SDK-default URL; hand-seeded for arcee-api); `None` for the
managed providers. An absent request `base_url` materializes to it
at settings resolution.

base_url.description:
The URL the models were actually read from, so the caller can persist
the same destination it validated against.

api_key_env.description:
Names a key already held in the environment or in NAC home, for a caller
that has one on file and no copy of the secret to send.

base_url.description: Overrides the provider's canonical URL, for a proxy or a custom gateway.

diagnostics.description:
Structural parse failures in the persisted values. These are diagnostics,
not migrations: callers must explicitly PATCH every invalid value.

oneOf.description: Light worker model; `None` keeps single-model dispatch.

message_idx.description:
Transcript index of the user message to answer again. It and everything
after it are dropped before the same prompt is submitted afresh.

oneOf.description: Compatibility form: a nonblank string containing a JSON object with string values.
Prefer an object of header names to values. The JSON-encoded string form is accepted for compatibility.

The optional light worker model of a session. `Some` on a session enables
weight-classified dispatch: light dispatches run this model, heavy
dispatches run the orchestrator's own model. The model remains a catalog
id; backend and reasoning effort are typed before entering the domain
model, and the credential is always a selector name, never a key value.
Cumulative usage from runs that produced no visible response.

message_idx.description:
Transcript index of the user message to go back to. That message and
everything after it are dropped.

SandboxActivity.description:
What sandbox setup is currently doing for one launching session, for UIs
waiting on a launch. Sandbox creation can take minutes (a first image
pull), and without this the only signal is a hung request.

SandboxAvailability.description:
The result of probing the sandbox runtime, with the steps that would make
it usable. Surfaced by the API so launch UIs can warn before a session
fails, and embedded in session-creation errors for agents driving the MCP.

detail.description: Why the runtime is unusable, when it is.

guidance.description: Platform-specific commands that would make it usable.

SandboxAvailabilityStatus.description: Whether the sandbox runtime (podman) can be used on this host right now.

activity_key.description:
Client-generated launch id used to key sandbox setup activity, so the
launching UI polls its own launch's progress. Deliberately not part of
`sandbox_requested`: it correlates progress reporting, nothing else.

SessionBehavior.description:
Immutable execution behavior selected when a top-level session is created.
Stored as text so future behaviors can fail closed instead of being
misinterpreted as the orchestrator.

oneOf.description:
Agent/model progress. The canonical top-level session busy lifecycle is
represented by RunStarted/RunCompleted/RunFailed/RunCancelled. AgentEvent
RunStarted/RunFinished remain low-level progress markers.

The run ended because the user asked it to, which is an outcome rather
than a fault. Carries no message: the user already knows what happened,
and the reason is a constant with nothing to report.

Live approval request for a prepared direct-session tool invocation.
The broker owns the pending state; this event lets web clients render
it without polling.

The waiting call ended without a user reply (for example cancellation
or timeout), so clients must remove the no-longer-actionable prompt.

Live-only signal that the orchestrator transcript log gained rows
(DB-direct transcript workset, step 3). `transcript_len` is the raw
merged transcript length after the append. Emitted at each transcript
commit point so subscribers refetch the store-backed transcript
mid-run. Never persisted: the bus persists only Agent events.

Live-only signal that a revert cut the transcript back to
`transcript_len` messages. Subscribers must refetch rather than apply a
delta: unlike an append, everything they hold past this point is gone.

deleted.description:
True when the forked session row is gone. The original chat still
shows the marker as a deleted item until the user dismisses it.

title.description: Live fork presentation title. Absent on a deleted fork.

SessionForkOrigin.description: The chat this session was forked from, for tab and list-row marks.

deleted.description: True when the original chat row is gone. The stored title still names it.

covered_orchestrator_steering_ids.description:
Delivered orchestrator steering records whose verbatim user message is
already present in the transcript source backing this snapshot. The
frontend hides those records so guidance renders exactly once — as the
canonical user message.

forks.description: Conversation forks created from a model turn in this session.

message_created_at.description:
When each message was written to the transcript log, aligned with
`messages`. `None` for messages carried by the snapshot blob, which
predates the log and stores no per-message time.

primary_tool_events.description:
Sanitized, bounded lifecycle events for top-level direct tool calls.
Kept separate from worker logs so primary calls cannot become a fake
delegated topology and the web never needs raw transcript payloads.

oneOf.description: Present when this chat was forked from another session.

run_count.description: Runs ever started in this session. Older stored snapshots default to 0.

ssh_host.description: OpenSSH/freeform target the session runs on; `None` = local session.

ssh_port.description:
Port and key the session was created with, so anything rebuilding the
connection reaches the same machine the same way. Omitted when the
session leaves them to ssh, which is what older snapshots always did.

total_cost_micros.description:
Micro-USD spend for the session. Omitted when no usage was recorded;
zero means the catalog had no rates for the model.

total_tokens.description:
Billable tokens accumulated over the session. Omitted when unknown, so
older stored snapshots keep deserializing.

SlashCommandDefinition.description: User-facing metadata shared by command parsing and frontend discovery.

SshBrowseRequest.description:
Where to look on an SSH host, for the remote half of the path picker.

The connection is described in the request rather than taken from a session,
because this is what the launch form asks *before* there is a session.

hidden.description: Dot-prefixed names are hidden unless explicitly requested, as locally.

path.description:
Absent or empty opens on the login home, which is where a fresh remote
session would start anyway.

SshConfigurationRecord.description: A named, reusable SSH connection offered by the launch modal.

last_four.description: Empty when the secret is too short for a suffix to be safe to show.

create.description: Make the branch first, off the current HEAD.

TestMcpServerRequest.description:
Probes a server before anything is saved. Either names a saved server or
carries the draft inline; inline map values may be null to borrow the
stored value when `stored_name` is also given.

TokenCostMicros.description:
Per-response cost in micro-USD (1e-6 USD), stored as u64 so `TokenUsage`
stays `Eq`. All-zero = unknown pricing (pi's zero-cost fallback). `total`
is the saturating sum of the four buckets, stored so consumers read it
directly. Missing fields deserialize as zero so partial records stay
loadable.

cost.description:
Per-response cost computed from catalog rates when the response was
parsed; zero when pricing is unknown. Serde-additive: rows persisted
before S3 deserialize with zero cost.

output_tokens.description:
Inclusive of `reasoning_tokens` — parsers normalize to the OpenAI
convention, and cost billing relies on it (reasoning bills at the
output rate via `max(output_tokens, reasoning_tokens)`).

total_tokens.description: Current context window size from the last ordinary orchestrator call.

extra_headers.description: Prefer a JSON object. Null or an empty object clears the persisted map.

light_model.description: Omitted preserves; null returns the session to single-model mode.

orchestrator_compaction_threshold.description: Omitted preserves; null or zero disables.

UpdateMcpServerRequest.description:
Edits a stored server in place. Every field is tri-state: omit it to keep
what is stored, send null to clear it, send a value to replace it.

`env` and `headers` replace the whole map when sent, except that a null
value under a key keeps the stored value for that key — the stored value
is never echoed back, so this is how an untouched secret survives an edit.

pinned.description:
Toggling this moves the project to the end of the target pin group and
bumps `presentation_version`.

UpdateSshConfigurationRequest.description:
Edits a saved SSH setup in place. Every field is tri-state: omit it to keep
what is stored, send null to clear it, send a value to replace it.

content.description: None whenever the file cannot be shown as text.

truncated.description: The repository has more files than were returned.

WorkspaceRevisionRecord.description:
One captured state of a session's checkout.

The heavy part of a revision — the files — lives in the repository as a git
commit; this row is only the bookkeeping that tells us which commit belongs
to which run, and what it should be compared against.

base_sha.description: The commit this revision is shown as a change against.

label.description: Prompt that started the run, for telling revisions apart in a list.

transcript_len.description:
How many transcript messages the session had when this revision was
taken — the link that lets a revert ask "what did the checkout look
like at this point in the conversation". `None` on rows written before
the column existed.
